description: This line plot illustrates the number of shared experts for two samples across six different task domains — Intent, Summary, Law, Translation, Code, and Math — as a function of increasing model scale, represented on the x-axis as powers of two from $2^9$ to $2^{20}$. The y-axis, labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” ranges from 2.0 to 6.0 and quantifies the average number of experts activated jointly by two distinct input samples within each task. The gray “Code” line starts at approximately 1.9 at $2^9$, dips slightly, then rises steadily to about 5.8 at $2^{20}$, showing the most pronounced growth. The blue “Summary” line begins near 2.0, rises sharply to 4.7 at $2^{11}$, dips to 4.5 at $2^{14}$, then climbs to ~5.9 at $2^{20}$. The orange “Intent” line starts around 3.8, peaks at ~5.5 at $2^{12}$, dips to 4.5 at $2^{14}$, then stabilizes near 6.0. The purple “Translation” line begins at 5.1, dips to 4.7 at $2^{11}$, then climbs steadily to ~5.9. The green “Math” line starts at 3.8, rises gradually to 5.9. The yellow “Law” line begins at 3.6, peaks at 5.8 at $2^{13}$, dips to 5.5 at $2^{14}$, then climbs to ~6.0. All lines converge near 5.9–6.0 at $2^{20}$, indicating saturation in shared expert usage at large scales.
